name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: A person born to a Kuwaiti father is Kuwaiti by origin, whether born inside or outside Kuwait, per the 2026 nationality-law amendments (Decree-Law No. 52 of 2026) confirming and restating this rule.

A child born to a Kuwaiti mother and a foreign father qualifies as Kuwaiti until age 21 if the father is deceased, imprisoned as a POW, or has divorced the mother -- a provision that, per the law firm alert reviewed, did not exist under the prior law. This is not a general gender-neutral descent rule: a child of a Kuwaiti mother and foreign father whose father is alive, not imprisoned, and still married to the mother does not qualify under this provision.

evidence_required.document: Proof of qualifying condition (maternal track): father's death certificate, POW status, or divorce decree

sources.title: Fragomen (global immigration law firm) -- summary of Kuwait's implemented 2025 nationality-law revisions: paternal descent restated for birth inside or outside Kuwait, and a new conditional maternal-descent provision (father deceased, POW, or divorced) for children under 21 that did not exist under the prior law

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kuwait). STATUS: DRAFT -- Kuwait's government gazette and the Ministry of Interior's own nationality pages were not fetchable in this build (403 errors, consistent with this country's other routes); sourced instead to a global immigration law firm's client alert (tier 3) describing the law AS IMPLEMENTED following 2024 cabinet approval and 2025-2026 enactment via Decree-Law No. 52 of 2026. LIVE LEGAL CONTEXT: Kuwait's nationality law has been under active, significant revision across 2024-2026 -- not a stable, long-settled framework like most other countries built in this dataset. The maternal-descent provision modeled here is a genuine partial improvement (it did not exist before) but remains narrow and conditional, not a general gender-neutral rule like Kenya, Pakistan, India, Tunisia, or Tanzania's reformed descent rules elsewhere in this dataset -- a child of a Kuwaiti mother whose foreign father is alive, free, and still married to her has no descent-based claim modeled here. dual_citizenship_allowed set false: Kuwait's nationality law has long barred dual citizenship for citizens by origin, and the 2026 amendments reportedly expand (rather than relax) revocation grounds tied to voluntary foreign-citizenship acquisition -- see kw_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes for the fuller revocation picture, which was not modeled as blocking requirements here since revocation is a POST-acquisition risk, not an acquisition condition.
